title: Uninvestment Check
concept: A quick check to tell the difference between someone needing space (still invested) and someone quietly pulling away for good — so you know which repair to reach for.
whenToUse: When warmth is missing even in ordinary moments, repairs feel like going through the motions, you've stopped planning ahead together, or contempt has replaced frustration.
steps: Each of you scores the signs below on your own, then share.
If it's just needing space → stick to Pause + Return and small repairs.
If three or more pulling-away signs show up → book a Full Recovery and set proof. Don't just wait it out.
If there's contempt, fear, or coercion → safety and outside support come first.
Set a time window to check if things are actually reinvesting.

phrases.text: I'm noticing some distance — do you just need space, or is something bigger going on?
I need a Full Recovery conversation; hope isn't a plan.
Contempt means we can't just carry on as normal.

working: Signs: fewer messages, only talking logistics, repairs feeling routine. The couple books a Full Recovery within a week, and tracks daily check-ins plus evening check-ins for 21 days. Things get clearer.
notWorking: Waiting for “them to miss me” while contempt keeps growing. Hoping instead of actually scheduling something just runs out the clock.
activity: Each of you marks, on your own: fewer check-ins that aren't just logistics, less curiosity about each other, avoiding future plans, doing more on your own, mostly practical conversations, going-through-the-motions affection, repairs that feel routine, contempt instead of frustration. Compare notes. If it points to pulling away, book a Full Recovery date before you leave the conversation.
warn: If contempt, fear, or coercion is present, safety and outside support come first.
